newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures plunges, CBOT corn lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures plunges, CBOT corn lower.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply lower on Thursday, with the three month down by its 500 yen limit, reflecting the Chicago market's price losses and the USDA's September crop report released overnight, traders said.
The January, the March and the May had fallen by the 500 yen limit by the close. Benchmark September 1997 was down 450 yen at 17,150 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 97,210 lots.

All months fell from the opening as local investors started selling, traders said. Price falls of the CBOT Project A corn trading during the Tokyo afternoon accelerated the bearish sentiment of yen-based corn futures, they said.

The USDA overnight said the 1996 U.S. corn crop would total 8.804 billion bushels, above its forecast in August of 8.695 billion. It also pegged 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.27 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimates of 2.24 billion.
The CBOT corn and soybean market continued to ease as selling orders from Asian traders emerged, traders said.
The December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.25-1/4 per bushel at 0755 GMT, against $3.26-3/4 at Wednesday's close.
The November of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $8.02 at 0820 GMT, against $8.05 from Wednesday's close.
